title: Prefix Sliding for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
hook: Most intermediate reasoning tokens stop mattering as the model reasons on. Keep only the prefix and the last few thousand tokens and you cap memory forever — 3x faster with no training.
key_points: Test-time scaling keeps the whole reasoning trace in memory via full attention, so long thinking gets prohibitively expensive.
The observation: most intermediate reasoning tokens lose importance as the model continues reasoning.
Prefix Sliding discards tokens outside the prefix and a window of the last few thousand tokens.
Total memory is capped regardless of how long the model reasons.
Without training it makes existing models 3x faster while maintaining performance.
Trained with RL, it enables scaling to reasoning traces beyond a hundred thousand tokens.
content_html: Test-time scaling buys accuracy with compute: let the model think longer. The bill comes from full attention, which keeps the entire reasoning trace in memory, so genuinely hard problems become prohibitively expensive. Muennighoff and colleagues make a simple observation that changes the arithmetic — most intermediate reasoning tokens lose importance as the model continues reasoning. So why keep paying for them?
extra_html:
The method

Prefix Sliding discards any token that is neither part of the prefix nor inside a window of the last few thousand tokens. The prefix retains the key instructions and the tools available to the model — the things that stay relevant to the end. The recent window holds the reasoning currently in progress. Everything in between is dropped. The consequence is structural: total memory is capped regardless of how long the model reasons, which is what makes genuinely long-horizon test-time scaling affordable.

Results

Applied without any training, Prefix Sliding makes existing models 3x faster while maintaining performance. Train with it using reinforcement learning and you get more: performance improves by enabling scaling to reasoning traces beyond a hundred thousand tokens. Ablations rule out the obvious alternatives — it outperforms both summarizing the intermediate tokens and a vanilla sliding window, so the preserved prefix is doing real work rather than the truncation alone. Code is released at github.com/Muennighoff/prefix-sliding. arXiv, 2026.

related.title: The KV Cache & Continuous Batching
related.hook: Generating one token reuses every prior key and value - that growing cache is why LLM inference is memory-bound, and continuous batching is how servers fight back.

related.title: PagedAttention / vLLM: Efficient LLM Serving
related.hook: LLM serving wastes huge amounts of GPU memory on the attention cache. PagedAttention borrows an OS trick — paging — to recover it and serve many more requests at once.

related.title: The Shadow Price of Reasoning
related.hook: When you can't afford to let every query think as long as it wants, who gets the compute? Treat reasoning tokens like a scarce resource and economics gives a clean answer.

related.title: The Draft Isn't Free at a Million Tokens
related.hook: Speculative decoding assumes the draft is cheap. At million-token context the draft head reads the entire KV cache every step — and can end up slower than no speculation at all.

flashcards.prompt: Which two spans of tokens does Prefix Sliding keep, and why those?
flashcards.back_html: The prefix, which holds key instructions and the tools available to the model, and a window of the last few thousand tokens, which is the reasoning currently being worked on. Everything between is discarded.

flashcards.prompt: What is the key empirical observation motivating Prefix Sliding?

choices.text: Most intermediate reasoning tokens lose importance as the model keeps reasoning
Attention weights are uniformly distributed over the reasoning trace
The first tokens of a reasoning trace are the least useful

flashcards.explanation_html: If old intermediate tokens stop mattering, paying full-attention memory to retain them is waste — which is exactly what Prefix Sliding stops paying.

flashcards.prompt: What do the ablations compare Prefix Sliding against?
flashcards.back_html: Summarizing the intermediate tokens, and a vanilla sliding window with no preserved prefix. Prefix Sliding outperforms both.

flashcards.prompt: What does training with Prefix Sliding via RL unlock beyond the training-free speedup?
flashcards.back_html: Better performance, by letting the model scale to reasoning traces beyond a hundred thousand tokens — because memory no longer grows with trace length.
